original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Which extra shape makes the executed helper mask E equal the forward footprint K on the three retained R439 helper-star words, while the synthetic restored edge fails that shape, and does the pinned degree-1 pair control satisfy it?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K contract and a paid profile. This package does not adopt one. It answers the released next question of the K-defect tally: name a hypothesis the three legal words satisfy and the synthetic edge violates, then test one other pinned helper-mixing word. Stop if the hypothesis is only that D was built to match K.
bottleneck_link: A legitimate H2/K replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit. Scalar agreement of two masks does not. The compensated-shear shape says when that agreement is forced, and the synthetic edge shows it is not free.
stop_rule: Stop once the compensated-shear shape is checked on the parent, the three tally words and the pair control, the one-edge identity is recorded, and the uncompensated probe and synthetic edge are shown to miss E. Do not adopt K_equals_D, price a new profile, or search another star forest.
evidence: verify.py checks the parent bracket, four descendant shapes, equality of E and K with the parent footprint, the one-edge identity on all 866 real edges plus five probe edges, one compensated probe, one uncompensated probe, and the three-gate synthetic edge.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance in the shape check, the verifier and the write-up. No proof assistant was used.

open_questions.question: Does every phase-B rewrite that keeps this D bracket preserve the forward helper footprint K, or only the three checked B/C variants?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The shear lemma fixes E. E equals K on those variants only because their changed B and C sections were checked to leave K unchanged.
open_questions.first_step: Take one other pinned B-section word with the same 306+111+306 transport blocks and compare its forward helper mask with the parent.
open_questions.blocked_by: No structural account of those B and C edits is claimed here, so a new word needs its own execution.

open_questions.question: After E is read as delivered columns, which H2 clause still fails on these words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Mask agreement does not repair the 612 target-to-target reads inside D. Adopting a contract still needs that clause.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate H2_D_frame0_targets_from_helpers on the star word and name the first failing read.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not rerun the owner interface checker and does not propose a replacement predicate.
